A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe the same Pretender research, with matching main sections and Appendices A-H. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and proofs support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original convergence experiments, quantitative comparisons on MovieLens, Last.fm, and Amazon, and a MovieLens case study.

after.justification: Section 6 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Figure 1 and Tables 1-2.

M1.justification: Pretender retains the same labeled-item preparation, continuous optimization, Bernoulli selection, and postprocessing procedure. Its MMD and Wasserstein variants are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MovieLens 100K, Last.fm, and Amazon-Home-and-Kitchen. The overlapping and disjoint MovieLens service scenarios and disjoint Last.fm and Amazon scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Random and Greedy in every corresponding comparison, together with the infeasible continuous optimum as a lower bound. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same service construction, preprocessing, Gaussian-kernel MMD evaluation, 1,000 Frank-Wolfe iterations, and 100 rounding trials. The K sweep from 1 to 128, K=100 quantitative comparison, and K=20 case study are unchanged.

E4.justification: The convergence analysis for MovieLens users 308 and 21, overlap comparison, and user-308 case study are retained without additional analyses. Appendices A-H remain theoretical proofs.

E5.justification: Table 1 reports the same means and standard deviations across users. Neither version adds experimental seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All Table 1 scores are unchanged, including Pretender's 0.1033 ± 0.040 MMD on MovieLens with intersection. Figure 1 retains identical curves, and Table 2 retains the same selected movies and feedback labels.

T1.justification: The substantive assumptions, guarantees, and derivations are unchanged, including all proofs in Appendices A-H. Corollary 3.6 corrects Z_D to Z_+, and Section 7 restores the minus sign in O(K^(-1/(d+2))); these repair notation to match the existing problem definition and Theorem 3.15.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same user-side cold-start formulation, Pretender algorithm, vanishing-error guarantees, and empirical effectiveness. The corrected exponent in the conclusion aligns its summary with the already-established theorem rather than introducing a stronger guarantee.

C2.justification: The metric tradeoffs, feature-mismatch limitation, and experimental interpretations are retained. Table 2's caption changes Cats Don't Dance being absent from the 'source' service to the 'target' service, matching the explanation already present in v1 Section 6.3.

D1.justification: V2 adds a Reproducibility statement after the introduction pointing readers to the Pretender code repository. V1 provides no corresponding code-access statement; the existing implementation and experimental details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 61 references and research positioning are retained. Adding 'quadrature' before 'methods based on the Frank-Wolfe algorithm' in Section 5.2 clarifies the existing context without changing the comparison with prior work.

P1.justification: V2 makes scattered spelling, grammar, and notation corrections, fixes the Section 6.2 reference from Table 2 to Table 1, and expands the acknowledgements. It also adds short publication, review, and reproducibility statements while retaining the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds a running publication header and a first-page review line, causing limited text reflow around the retained displays. Table 2's caption is corrected, while Figure 1 and both tables retain their visual structure and contents.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a concrete code-access pointer and corrects misleading cross-reference, caption, and concluding exponent errors. These changes modestly improve reproducibility documentation and internal consistency; the method, empirical evidence, and substantive theory remain unchanged.
